text:
Priya (security): Alert: automated detector flagged potential AWS access keys embedded in an unencrypted Terraform state file in a public S3 bucket. Were treating this as high-priority exposure.

Jules (infra): Ugh. Which bucket?

Priya (security): Bucket: `redwood-terraform-prod-backups-2024`. Object path: `states/us-west-2/infra/2024-11-02.tfstate`. Scanner found patterns matching access_key_id / secret_access_key.

Rui (qa): How confident is the detector? False positives happen with snapshots.

sec-bot: Confidence: 92%. Matched regex for AWS access key ID and AWS secret key format. Sample lines redacted in the report.

Priya (security): Immediate actions (TL;DR): revoke any exposed keys, rotate creds used by terraform runners, make state file private/encrypted, enable MFA/enforced session policies for any affected principals. Follow checklist below.

Asha (platform): That bucket should have been private + SSE-KMS. Who owns that backup job?

Jules (infra): That backup job is managed by `infra/backup-runner` (service account `svc-infra-backup@redwood`). Looks like a misconfigured lifecycle copy to a backup bucket that got public-read by mistake via a lifecycle rule added in Sept.

Priya (security): Checklist (do now):
- Owners: take bucket offline or set block-public-access and remove public ACLs immediately.
- Rotate any AWS keys whose id appears in the detection report. Use the IAM console or `rwdctl iam rotate-key --id <key-id>` and mark as incident-rotated.
- Revoke any sessions for principals tied to those keys: `rwdctl auth revoke-sessions --principal svc-infra-backup`
- Replace terraform state with sanitized version (remove creds), re-encrypt with KMS, and set ACL to private.
- Run the forensic scan across backup buckets: see command below.

Jules (infra): I'm revoking ACLs and blocking public access now.

DevOps-bot: Action taken: blocked public access on `redwood-terraform-prod-backups-2024` at 2024-11-03T14:12:10Z.

Priya (security): Forensic scan (example):
```bash
# list objects and grep for AWS key patterns (dry-run, use from security workstation)
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-terraform-prod-backups-2024 --prefix states/ --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text | \ 
  xargs -n1 -I{} aws s3 cp s3://redwood-terraform-prod-backups-2024/{} - | \ 
  grep -E "(AKIA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}|(?i)aws_secret_access_key" -n || true
```

Rui (qa): We should also run CI test to ensure no pipelines consume plaintext creds. I'll audit pipeline variables for `infra/backup-runner`.

Asha (platform): We'll flip the backup job to use the platform short-lived OIDC token flow and update docs.

Priya (security): Timeline:
- Immediate (0-2h): block public access, snapshot object, start key rotation.
- Short (2-24h): rotate any exposed keys, revoke sessions, update terraform state, postmortem ticket created.
- Medium (24-72h): audit other buckets, update backup job to OIDC, enable KMS SSE and bucket-level encryption, add automated alerts.

Jules (infra): I've rotated the service-account keys and disabled the old access key (ID ends with ABCD). Will post details to the ticket.

DevOps-bot: Key rotation: `svc-infra-backup` access key `AKIA...ABCD` disabled at 2024-11-03T14:25:03Z. New key created and stored in Vault path `secret/infra/backup/svc-infra-backup` (owner: infra).

Priya (security): Good. Owners: file an incident ticket with label `sec:tfstate-exposure` and include: affected bucket, exposed key IDs, principal names, revocation evidence, and remediation timeline. Post the ticket link here once created.

Rui (qa): Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4821 (private). Adding remediation checklist and owners.

sec-bot: Automated scan: queued full backup-buckets audit. Report ETA: 3 hours. Alerts will post to #eng-security.

Asha (platform): We'll schedule a config review to remove any lifecycle rule that can change ACLs or copy to public buckets. Also adding PR check to block public ACLs on bucket creation.

Priya (security): Follow-up required:
- All teams with any terraform state backups: confirm encryption and private ACL within 48h.
- Platform: add pre-commit/pre-merge check to reject bucket ACL changes that make them public.
- SRE: increase alerting on public bucket changes.

Jules (infra): Noted, I'll coordinate with product infra to push the PRs.

Priya (security): Thanks. If you find additional exposed secrets while auditing, tag them in the same ticket. If blocked, ping me directly with `sec:urgent`. :lock:
